comparator.name: Astronomy (Sterrenkunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026-27 Leiden Study Guide and public product API define a 180-EC Astronomy bachelor with 60 EC of compulsory courses in each of years one and two. Year three contains 8 EC of further compulsory astronomy and research-skills study, a 22-EC bachelor research project, and 30 EC of restricted elective space. To instantiate that space as one broad astronomy-centred pathway, the selection combines Astro-Particle Physics, Astrobiology, Astronomy from Space, Astronomical Relativity, Bayesian Statistics for Astrophysics, Mathematical Methods of Physics and Relativistic Electrodynamics. These options cover astronomical phenomena, theory and quantitative methods, total exactly 30 EC, and were selected from the official list independently of UCR fit. All components together account for exactly 180 EC.

exception.reason: Leiden's Astronomy bachelor requires a continuous mathematical and physical foundation, dedicated astrophysics and planetary-systems study, practical observing and laboratory work, quantum mechanics, electrodynamics, stellar and galactic astrophysics, cosmology, specialist astronomy electives and a 22-EC independent astronomy research project. UCR offers useful mathematics, programming and data-science courses, but no astronomy or astrophysics course, no classical or quantum physics sequence, no astronomical observing course and no physics or astronomy laboratory. A 24-course response assembled from mathematics, computing, earth science and general natural science would replace Astronomy with adjacent tools and topics rather than implement its academic core.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official 2026-27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC: a 60-EC compulsory first year; a 60-EC compulsory second year; and a third year containing 8 EC of required Radiative Processes and research integrity, a 22-EC bachelor research project, and a coherent instantiated 30-EC astronomy-centred elective package. The programme has no named graduation route. Its identity is a cumulative theory-observation-computation-research progression in astronomy, astrophysics, mathematics and physics.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide mathematical tools; DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming and the data-science sequence provide computational methods. ENSENVI111 Dynamic Earth addresses geology and geophysics, while other natural-science courses concern biology, chemistry, sustainability or engineering applications. The workbook contains no course in astronomy, astrophysics, planetary systems, classical mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, statistical physics or cosmology, and no astronomical observing or physics-laboratory sequence. The adjacent mathematical and computational courses cannot give 23 non-PPD courses a concrete Astronomy rationale or reproduce the external theory-to-research progression.
